newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-D&B Australia Q4 business survey summary.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-D&B Australia Q4 business survey summary.

text.p: The following is a summary of Dun & Bradstreet's fourth quarter 1996 Australian business expectations survey.

Sales growth expectations have increased three points to 37; although sales expectations for non-durables manufacturers fell eight points, they are still more optimistic than executives in the other sectors. For durables manufacturers the index rose one point and for wholesalers, two points. Retailers have become more optimistic; their expected sales index rose 11 points to 40, the best outlook for growth in retail sales since the beginning of 1995.

New orders expectations have advanced two points and are now 23 points above the low point for the first quarter of 1996. Non-durables manufacturers new orders expectations are very strong having risen a further three points to 54. Orders expectations for wholesalers have advanced one point to an index of 35. Durables manufacturers' new orders expectations are much weaker.

Expectations for higher profits have returned to an index of 24, a level they were at two quarters ago. Non durables manufacturers are still the most optimistic about profits but have decreased their optimism by eight points to an index of 36. Wholesalers' profits expectations are now the least optimistic, four points below the retailers' index of 24.

The net proportion of firms expecting to raise their selling prices remained unchanged at 13 percent. The rise in the retail and durables manufacturing sectors being balanced by the fall in prices expectations in wholesaling and non-durables. The index for wholesalers is just six and equal to the lowest level recorded by wholesalers in nine years. Selling price expectations for non-durables manufacurers fell nine points.

Employment expectations were unchanged at an index of seven, the rise in expectations by retailers of five points, balancing the falls of one or two points in the other sectors. Retailers are the most positive about growth in the number of their employees.

Inventories expectations have increased by five points to an index of eight, with 31 percent expecting an increase, 23 percent a decrease, and 46 percent no change. Durables manufacturers are the only group expecting a reduction in their inventories, with 30 percent expect to decrease inventories and only 22 percent to increase inventories.

Expectations for increases in capital investment remained unchanged at an index of 17 with 27 percent of firms expecting an increase and 10 percent a decrease. Non-durables manufacturers are the most optimistic about rises in capital investment.

NOTE: The index figures used represent the net percentage of survey respondents compared with the same quarter of the privious year. The indices are calculated by subtracting the percentage of respondents expecting decreases from the percentage expecting increases. The survey of about 900 business owners and senior executives from major industry sectors was conducted in September.
